children.topic: On Admission
Key Event / Landmark: Diagnosis (2 out of 3 Atlanta Criteria)
Imaging of Choice: Right Upper Quadrant (RUQ) Ultrasound to evaluate for gallstones
Management Principle: Supportive care: aggressive IV crystalloid resuscitation, analgesics (pethidine), NPO
Within 48 Hours
Key Event / Landmark: Triage and severity assessment
Imaging of Choice: Chest X-ray (classically evaluates for left-sided pleural effusion)
Management Principle: Utilize Ranson’s Criteria (GA LAW / CHOBBS) or BISAP
Day 3 to 7
Key Event / Landmark: Failure to clinically improve or clinical deterioration
Imaging of Choice: Abdominal CT scan with contrast to look for pancreatic necrosis
Management Principle: Re-evaluate; transition to enteral nutrition past the ligament of Treitz if kept NPO > 7 days
Hospital Week 3 to 4
Key Event / Landmark: Delayed sepsis, fever, and leukocytosis
Imaging of Choice: Contrast-Enhanced CT (non-enhancing necrosis + gas bubbles)
Management Principle: Step-Up Approach: Imipenem, CT-guided FNA, percutaneous drain -> VARD -> Necrosectomy
Post-Op Week 6
Key Event / Landmark: Vague pain, early satiety, epigastric fullness
Imaging of Choice: Abdominal CT scan (thin-walled fluid collection in lesser sac)
Management Principle: Internal Drainage (Cystogastrostomy or Cystojejunostomy)
